html:
SMTO-UI-0023 — This model setting needs an ordinary number

GUID: 650ebb61-95e2-4f27-943e-aedeca60d7e7
Slug: ui-number-invalid
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • The value you typed for one of the model's number settings can't be used as a normal number, for example because it's far too large. SMTO didn't accept the change.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the model and find the setting that has the message under it. The message appears right under the setting with the unusable value.
  2. Type a plain number such as 0.7 or 4096, without letters, extra symbols or very long strings of digits. Huge or malformed values can't be turned into a normal number the model understands.
  3. If you're unsure, open its Help and use the Explicit starting value, or turn the switch off. Then select Save for that model. The starting value is a known good number, and turning the switch off uses the provider's default.

What success looks like

  • The message under the setting disappears and the model saves.

If it still fails

  • Turn the setting's switch off to use the provider default, and send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO's model setup.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A numeric model parameter input converted to a non-finite JavaScript number (Infinity or NaN), so the model configuration editor rejected the change.

What this means

  • Numeric input converts to a non-finite JavaScript number. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Numeric input converts to a non-finite JavaScript number.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the input syntax rather than accepting infinity or an invalid numeric conversion.

How to fix it

  • In model_configuration.js the input change handler throws ui_number_invalid when Number(input.value) is not finite (for example 1e999 overflows to Infinity). Enter a finite value that also passes the parameter's integer and minimum/maximum checks, or turn the override off.
  • Enter a finite number in the indicated field.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A finite number passes the field's additional schema checks.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
